lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A three-goal hole became a springboard, and suddenly the Maple Leafs have a rookie's first star turn to go with a needed jolt of belief. Toronto rallied past Nashville 5-4 in overtime Tuesday, with Gavin McKenna scoring his first NHL goal and adding an assist. The 18-year-old's top-corner finish, set up by Auston Matthews, announced that the No. 1 pick is no longer merely a promising name on the lineup sheet. Matthews supplied the ending, scoring with 14 seconds left in overtime, while Toronto moved to 2-2-0 and held second place in the Atlantic Division with four points. That is progress, not proof; the Leafs have traded wins and losses all season. Still, a comeback like this can harden a room. Next comes Thursday's 10 p.m. ET visit to Vegas, where McKenna's encore - and Toronto's ability to defend a lead before needing heroics - will matter.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and 79-83 leaves Toronto with more questions than excuses after a fifth-place finish in the AL East. Now the meaningful work begins. Jake Casey's three-steal Arizona Fall League showcase on October 7 offered a small but vivid reminder that the organization still has speed and athleticism in the pipeline, even if the No. 23 prospect remains hitless to start the fall. His 13 home runs and .504 slugging percentage in 2026 suggest tools worth developing, while his 28.1% strikeout rate demands patience. The larger decision sits atop the rotation: Kevin Gausman is a free agent, and a shorter, cheaper reunion could restore a trusted veteran without recreating an aging contract. Watch whether Toronto turns that possibility into a priority - and whether Casey's development can accelerate a roster that needs both youth and certainty.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' preseason has already delivered its warning label: talent is not the same thing as readiness. The 129-105 exhibition loss to Miami on October 3 exposed a group still searching for its shape, though the score counts for nothing in the standings. The real story is Kawhi Leonard, who is back in Toronto and choosing patience over theater - taking contact, learning a new system and resisting the urge to make October prove anything. That restraint matters. Toronto has learned to win without him, and it may need that muscle again. The projected core of Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl remains enticing, but Collin Murray-Boyles and others are pressing for minutes, while roster decisions sharpen. Saturday's preseason meeting with the Clippers is the next test - watch the rotation, not the scoreboard, and whether Leonard's slow integration becomes the season's defining advantage.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The London loss did more than dent the record - it ripped open Washington's injury ledger. Sunday's 30-13 defeat to Indianapolis left Marcus Mariota without a timeline after another MCL sprain and Jaylin Lane lost for the season, turning a bad afternoon into a roster crisis. At 1-3, the Commanders sit fourth in the NFC East, two games back, with a one-game losing streak and little margin for another stumble. The one bright beam is Jayden Daniels, expected to return to practice and start against New York after missing time with an elbow injury. He is not a cure-all, but Washington badly needs his legs, judgment and authority. The Giants arrive 3-1 and freshly sharpened by their underdog "humbling." Sunday's 1 p.m. meeting on Fox is Washington's chance to stop the slide before October turns a rough start into a lost season.

article.title: McKenna Scores First Goal as Leafs Beat Predators
paragraphs: Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal Tuesday as the Maple Leafs beat Nashville 5-4, completing a comeback that also featured a four-point night from Auston Matthews. William Nylander had a goal and two assists, while Anthony Stolarz made 21 saves. Toronto is 2-2-0 and visits the Golden Knights Thursday at 10:00 p.m. ET on TSN.

The Jays are looking ahead, with outfield prospect Casey drawing attention in the Arizona Fall League and Kevin Gausman's possible return being discussed. The Raptors play the Clippers in a preseason game Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET before opening the regular season against the Bulls on October 21. Kawhi Leonard is taking time to integrate into Toronto's lineup.
The Commanders are 1-3 and host the Giants Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Washington lost cornerback Terrell Smith when Pittsburgh signed him from the practice squad.
